findings: 1,200 synthetic customers previewed in 50.482 seconds and applied in 81.724 seconds. Exactly 1,200 people, cards, source links, row outcomes and provenance records were retained.

Completed replay returned HTTP 200 and did not change counts/attempts. The first harness incorrectly expected top-level status; the implemented response carries import.status. The harness was corrected; authenticated row-window/card-pagination assertions were not reached in that trial.
The advertised 5,000-row preview failed HTTP 546 after 132.325 seconds. It left no saved import, canonical records or outcomes. The precise server-side resource limit was not determined.
Both fixtures retired their temporary login/write authority, retained evidence and matched all 18 pre-existing source/card table fingerprints.
Current code makes one database RPC per matched/applied row. Bounded database batches are the next candidate; they are not installed or used by the hosted endpoint.
limitations: Synthetic customer imports only; no real package or provider traffic.
